sections.label: CPF and Singtel SDS transfer
sections.summary: The CPF is a key pillar of Singapore's social security system, and this update transfers Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to CDP accounts of SDS holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The CPF is a key pillar of Singapore's social security system and has been updated over the years to meet our members' changing needs and ensure its continued effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: It updates a legacy arrangement by enabling the transfer of Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to the Central Depository (CDP) accounts of SDS holders.

sections.label: SDS holders and holdings
sections.summary: Before April, there were around 615,000 SDS holders, whose holdings were under 5% of Singtel's total shareholdings, with the median holder having about 1,360 shares worth about $6,800.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Prior to the start of this exercise in April, there were around 615,000 SDS holders, whose SDS holdings collectively represented less than 5% of Singtel's total shareholdings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The median SDS holder had around 1,360 shares that were worth about $6,800 in equity value.

sections.label: Bill amends CPF Act
sections.summary: The Bill amends the CPF Act to automatically transfer the shares to CDP accounts under the SDS holders' names, making the process seamless.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Bill amends the CPF Act to effect the automatic transfer of the shares to CDP accounts under the respective SDS holders' names, thereby ensuring that the process is seamless for SDS holders.

sections.label: SDS sale proceeds withdrawal
sections.summary: The CPF Board decided to let SDS holders who sell their SDS withdraw proceeds in cash without meeting CPF withdrawal conditions, effected from 8 April 2026, with around seven months before the November transfer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Given that the SDS scheme has achieved its objective of allowing SDS holders to benefit and share in Singapore's development, the CPF Board has reviewed its rules and decided to allow those who sell their SDS to withdraw their proceeds in cash if they wish to do so without having met CPF withdrawal conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We have effected this from 8 April 2026 through subsidiary legislation amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: SDS holders have ample time of around seven months to decide if they want to sell their shares before the planned transfer in November.

sections.label: SDS holders needing assistance
sections.summary: Over 20,000 SDS holders who may require greater assistance have been identified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In addition, we have identified over 20,000 SDS holders who may require greater assistance.

sections.label: Singtel SDS transfer to CDP
sections.summary: CPF members who bought discounted Singtel SDS made significant gains, and this Bill transfers Singtel SDS from the CPF Board to CDP accounts so holders can manage shares directly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: CPF members who have purchased the discounted Singtel SDS have made significant gains over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This Bill updates a legacy arrangement by transferring Singtel SDS from CPF Board to individual CDP accounts or designated CDP accounts of SDS holders, thus allowing those who prefer to keep their Singtel SDS, to hold and manage their shares directly.

sections.label: SDS holders transfer impact
sections.summary: About 615,000 SDS holders are affected; the median holder paid about $2,000, shares worth about $6,800 as at April, with about $5,000 cumulative dividends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: About 615,000 SDS holders will be affected by this transfer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The median SDS holder paid about $2,000 for the shares; they are worth about $6,800 as at April and have received about $5,000 in cumulative dividends.

sections.label: SDS holders age profile
sections.summary: Many SDS holders are older, the youngest in their 50s, and about half are 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Many SDS holders are older, indeed, the youngest are in their 50s, and about half are 65 and above.

sections.label: CPF scam prevention measures
sections.summary: CPF Board sent notification letters, set up a dedicated hotline and conducted door-to-door visits for vulnerable SDS holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Does CPF Board expect an uptick in related scams and how will it pre-empt them?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I note CPF Board has sent notification letters, set up a dedicated hotline and conducted door-to-door visits for vulnerable SDS holders.

sections.label: SDS value and CPF rules
sections.summary: A $2,000 Singtel SDS investment grew to nearly $12,000, outperforming the CPF Ordinary Account, and under section 26E(2) dividends and sale proceeds must be returned to CPF while shares remain in the designated shares account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The illustration, as shared by the CPF board in Singtel is clear – for the median SDS holder with approximately 1,360 Singtel SDS shares, a $2,000 investment in Singtel SDS has grown into nearly $12,000 in total value today, comprising $5,000 in cumulative dividends and $6,800 worth of shares as at 1 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In contrast, had that same $2,000 remain in the CPF Ordinary Account, earning a base interest of 2.5%, it will be worth only approximately $4,500 today, a mere 38% of the value of the SDS shares, or in other words, the SDS has outperformed the CPF Ordinary Account by a factor of 2.6 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, I note that under section 26E(2) of the Bill, while shares remain in the designated shares account, dividends and sale proceeds must be returned to the CPF Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, once the shares are transferred to a direct CDP account and sold, the funds do not need to be returned to the CPF.

sections.label: Middle household wealth composition
sections.summary: The middle 20% of households hold most household wealth in property equity, 33% in net CPF balances and only 14% in other financial equity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The middle 20% of households have the majority of their household wealth in property equity, followed by 33% in net CPF balances and only 14% in other financial equity.

sections.label: CPF investment growth and schemes
sections.summary: A $2,000 CPF investment grew to nearly $12,000 including $5,000 in accumulated dividends, more than twice the return from the CPF Ordinary Account at 2.5% interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A $2,000 CPF investment made at the time has grown to a total value of nearly $12,000 today, including $5,000 in accumulated dividends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For many Singaporeans, this represents a substantial contribution to their retirement savings, and more importantly, it is more than twice the return that would have been earned by leaving the money in a CPF Ordinary Account at 2.5% interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Had the Government fulfilled its promise to extend similar discounted share schemes to companies, such as PUB, SMRT and PSA, would our retirement security be considerably more robust today?

sections.label: SDS transfer and CPF waiver
sections.summary: The amendment facilitates transferring SDS from the CPF Board to the CDP, waiving CPF withdrawal conditions and letting shareholders withdraw proceeds in cash.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The amendment before us facilitates the transfer of SDS from the CPF Board to the CDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But crucially, for this transfer exercise, CPF withdrawal conditions will be waived and shareholders have the option of withdrawing proceeds in cash.

sections.label: Early drawdown of retirement savings
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the cash-out waiver unintentionally encourages early drawdown of retirement savings, especially as the Basic Retirement Sum rises to $110,200.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: By allowing this cash-out waiver, we must ask ourselves: are we unintentionally encouraging those who can least afford it to drawdown on retirement savings too early, especially as the Basic Retirement Sum raises to $110,200 this year.

sections.label: MRSS top-ups and matching
sections.summary: With an average shareholding of about $6,800, eligible seniors making gradual MRSS top-ups over several years could see savings effectively doubled through Government matching.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: With an average shareholding of about $6,800, eligible seniors who make gradual MRSS top-ups over several years could potentially see these savings effectively doubled through Government matching.

sections.label: Automatic MRSS matching proposal
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to consider automatic MRSS matching for eligible shareholders who sweep part of proceeds into CPF retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider automatic MRSS matching for eligible shareholders who voluntarily choose to sweep part of their proceeds into their CPF retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This would reduce administrative hassles and help strengthen retirement adequacy for lower balanced members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Let us do better for our most vulnerable seniors.

sections.label: CPF Amendment Bill transfer procedure
sections.summary: The CPF (Amendment) Bill is procedural, facilitating transfer of designated shares like Singtel SDS through CDP Accounts, letting shareholders receive sale proceeds in cash or direct them to CPF Ordinary Accounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The CPF (Amendment) Bill is in many ways a procedural Bill aimed at facilitating the transfer of designated shares, notably the Singtel SDS, first through CDP Accounts in individual investors' names.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will then allow such shareholders the option of either choosing to receive proceeds from their sale in cash or to direct them back to their CPF Ordinary Accounts.

sections.label: Cash payout and scam risk
sections.summary: The speaker notes clause 12 establishes CDP accounts for about 40% of shareholders who never actively traded equities, and clause 6 allows direct cash payout, raising fraud and scam risks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Onto less morbid points, my second point relates to the interaction of clause 12 of the Bill, which establishes CDP accounts for the estimated 40% of shareholders who have never otherwise actively traded equities, with clause 6, which allows a direct cash payout of sales proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Alas, the increased flexibility of allowing the withdrawal of equity sales proceeds were well meaning, also means that there could be a double-edged sword with unscrupulous fraudsters and scammers, potentially already licking the teeth at the prospect of accessing this pool of previously locked up funds.

sections.label: Singtel discounted shares debate
sections.summary: The Government said offering discounted Singtel shares aimed to let Singaporeans share in a national asset and promote widespread share ownership.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, in the debate surrounding the Telecommunications Authority of Singapore Bill, which formalised the privatisation of Singtel and allocated discounted shares to CPF shareholders, the Government of the time declared that its intention for offering such discounted shares was to, and I quote, "give an opportunity to share in the success of a national asset, promote long term widespread share ownership, and give Singaporeans a direct stake in the country's success." These are laudable goals and one that even today many of us can get behind.

sections.label: Singtel discounted share take-up
sections.summary: In 1993, 1.45 million Singaporeans, about 86% of those eligible, accepted the discounted A share offer, and 1.53 million took up a 1996 tranche.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, this was arguably already achieved back in 1993, when 1.45 million Singaporeans, or about 86% of those eligible accepted the discounted A share offer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet the Government went ahead with a second discounted tranche of Singtel in 1996, where 1.53 million citizens happily took up the secondary offering.

sections.label: Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme
sections.summary: The Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme is scheduled for 2028, with more legislation expected and interest in greater CPF account holder involvement in the local stock market.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: CPFIS, is a mouthful, is not novel, but at the top of mind for most policy observers must be the impending Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme scheduled for 2028.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe that more legislation specific to the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme is to follow, and there is a fair degree of excitement over how a more explicit involvement of CPF account holders in the local stock market might further revive the SGX's fortunes.

sections.label: Transferring shares to individuals
sections.summary: Transferring ownership of these shares from the CPF Board to individual holders and integrating them into the Central Depository system is described as logical and forward-looking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In that regard, transferring ownership of these shares from the CPF Board to individual holders and integrating them into the Central Depository system, is a logical and forward-looking step.

sections.label: Control over CPF shares
sections.summary: Singaporeans will have full control over these assets, including liquidating them and withdrawing cash freely instead of keeping sales proceeds in the CPF Ordinary Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Singaporeans will now have full control over these assets, including the ability to liquidate them and withdraw cash freely, rather than retaining their sales proceeds in the CPF Ordinary Account.

sections.label: Scams and mis-selling risk
sections.summary: The passage states that the heightened risk of scams and mis-selling is of particular concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Third, and of particular concern, is the heightened risk of scams and mis-selling.

sections.label: Consumer share sale safeguards
sections.summary: A first-time share sale could include a clear prompt or a short cooling-off period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: For example, when a consumer attempts to sell their shares for the first time, there could be a clear prompt or a short cooling-off period.

sections.label: Support for Bill, equity stake
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and notes about 615,000 Singaporeans received a direct equity stake in economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I support the Bill, but I have a few clarifications and suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It gave more than 600,000 – in fact, about 615,000 Singaporeans today – a direct equity stake in our nation's economic growth.

sections.label: SDS holders without CDP accounts
sections.summary: The speaker asks how many SDS holders do not have CDP accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For those without CDP accounts, how many SDS holders fall into this group?

sections.label: Safeguards for seniors, SDS sales
sections.summary: The speaker asks about safeguards for seniors and how many SDS holders sold shares or withdrew cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What safeguards are in place to protect, in particular, seniors from scams or financial exploitation during this transition?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share how many SDS holders have sold their shares since the announcement and how many have withdrawn proceeds in cash versus retaining them within CPF?

sections.label: Support for CPF Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, saying the CPF Board need no longer be trustee for SDS and the sunset approach is fair and prudent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I support the Central Provident Fund (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There is no longer a need for the CPF Board to serve as a trustee for Singaporeans' SDS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Government's approach to sunset this programme is fair and it is prudent.

sections.label: Closing CPFIS Special Account
sections.summary: The speaker suggests closing the CPF Investment Scheme for the Special Account and renaming the Special Account the Retirement Account from day one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In my view, it is time to consider closing the CPF Investment Scheme for the Special Account, where three out of four who invested through the scheme have been worse off compared to leaving their savings in the Special Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In fact, taking it a step further, the Special Account itself should just be called the Retirement Account from day one, instead of the current system where the Special Account is closed and the Retirement Account is created at age 55.

sections.label: SDS scheme objectives and extension
sections.summary: The SDS scheme is a legacy scheme with no plans to extend it as of now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: Mr Loh also asked whether the SDS scheme has achieved its original objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: Also, in response to Mr Louis Chua's comments, the SDS scheme is a legacy scheme rooted in a very specific context of its time and there are no plans to extend this scheme as of now.

sections.label: SDS participation and returns
sections.summary: Over a million members joined the voluntary SDS scheme in 1993 and 1996, with returns up to six times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: Over the two tranches in 1993 and 1996, over a million members chose to participate in this voluntary SDS scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: SDS holders have also benefited from returns of up to six times, not inclusive of interest earned on dividends.

sections.label: SDS holders selling shares
sections.summary: As of end April, around 81,000 SDS holders, or 13%, have sold their shares.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: As of end April, around 81,000 SDS holders, or 13%, have sold their shares.

sections.label: SDS sale channels and charges
sections.summary: Singtel SDS can be sold through channels like Phillip Securities at the same rates, with sales process and charges unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: Singtel SDS, including odd lots, can be sold through channels such as Phillip Securities at the same rates as today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: On Mr Fadli Fawzi's question about charges, the sales process and charges during the period are the same as what they were prior to the exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: SDS holders are not limited to selling via SingPost or Phillip Securities as it is up to the Singapore Exchange brokers whether or not they wish to facilitate the sale of Singtel SDS, which also includes costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: I also wanted to add at this point that for members, particularly the seniors who go to SingPost outlets, about 95% of sales transactions are actually done online by them, and therefore, circumventing the need to even pay the $17 that was raised by Mr Fadli.

sections.label: SDS sale assistance locations
sections.summary: SDS holders may go to more than 30 SingPost branches or five CPF Service Centres for assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: SDS holders may go to more than 30 SingPost branches for assistance with the sale of their shares, or any of the five CPF Service Centres for general assistance.

sections.label: SDS notification and proceeds rules
sections.summary: Notification letters go only to verified addresses, and sale proceeds are credited only to registered bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: First, the personalised notification letters containing each SDS holder's specific details will be sent only to their verified addresses on record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: Second, sale proceeds will be credited only to SDS holders' bank account registered with the CPF Board or via their PayNow-NRIC registered bank account.

sections.label: Singtel SDS holders' backgrounds
sections.summary: About 70% of Singtel SDS account holders were from HDB background, including the speaker, and 30% from the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: It was precisely that, and I think Singaporeans had responded positively to Mr Goh's clarion call back then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: I am also happy to state that as far as the Singtel SDS is concerned, that almost 70% of people who have the SDS Singtel accounts were from HDB background and dwelling, including myself, and 30% belong to the private sector.

sections.label: SDS transfer benefits and options
sections.summary: With the transfer, SDS holders gain greater control, and those not wishing to participate can realise decades of capital gains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: With the transfer, SDS holders will benefit from greater control and those who do not wish to participate in the transfer can also choose to realise their capital gains that they have made, over the decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister of State Dinesh, unlike you and the rest of those who spoke, I am happy to say that I am old enough to have received the Singtel shares.      .
